capitals.note: The page has Sultan Murad retreat to Diyar Bakr after 1501 and the Safavids take Diyarbakir in 1507-08; my reading of the seat.

correction.text: the Bayburt district where the page attests the confederation

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria starts in 1407 but the page dates the confederation from 1378 ('ruled eastern Turkey from 1378 to 1508'), attested in the Bayburt district from the 1340s (first raid on Trebizond 1340, failed siege 1348). The lead says 'founded in the Diyarbakir region', but Diyar Bakr is Timur's grant of 1402, so the earlier core is drawn at Bayburt.

correction.text: Diyar Bakr as granted by Timur in 1402, the Diyarbakir governorship including Mardin

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'Timur granted them Diyar Bakr in 1402'; Âmid capital from 1403; Cliopatria's first shape begins in 1407. Mardin was part of the Diyarbakır governorship given to Kara Yülük Osman (Uzun Hasan page).
56,839 km2 around Diyarbakir, Mardin, Sanliurfa, Bingol and Batman: matches Timur's 1402 grant of Diyar Bakr. The page gives no area, so the infobox comparison is impossible.
77,464 km2: the 1407 shape plus about 20,000 km2 in Raqqa and Hasakah (Syria). Unverified: page budget; no page dates the extension (event at confidence 1).

correction.text: Diyar Bakr and the Syrian Jazira edge without Iraq and Khuzestan

keyframe_review.note: 233,300 km2 adds Iraq (Babil, Karbala, Qadisiyyah and more) and Khuzestan, the same corner of the map as the Cliopatria 'Hashemite Arab Federation' row of 1415-1439 (lower Iraq and Khuzestan). The pages put Iraq in Qara Qoyunlu hands: Jahan Shah captured Baghdad on 9 June 1446 and held 'most of present-day Iraq' (Jahan Shah page; Qara Qoyunlu page: Baghdad captured 1410). The Aq Qoyunlu of 1440-1452 held only Diyar Bakr (the page's capital Âmid 1403-1468). Correction removes Iraq and Khuzestan (about 91,000 km2 remain). Reviewed again 2026-10-25 for the thin finding: no page opened gives Aq Qoyunlu holdings for 1435-1452 beyond Diyar Bakr. The Uzun Hasan page has Timur appoint Kara Yuluk Osman governor of Diyarbakir 'with Erzincan, Mardin, Ruha (Urfa) and Sivas' (no year) and has Uzun Hasan seize Amid in a bloodless coup in autumn 1452 while Jahangir was in Kurdistan; the Aq Qoyunlu page adds nothing for these years. The Mamluk Sultanate page says that after the Mamluk sack of Edessa (1429) and attack on Amid (1433) 'The Aq Qoyonlu consequently recognized Mamluk suzerainty': it gives no year for the recognition and no end (it records only the 1472 Aq Qoyunlu expedition around Aleppo, routed by Yashbak), while the Aq Qoyunlu and Uzun Hasan pages never mention Mamluk suzerainty (the Aq Qoyunlu page calls Uzun Hasan Qaitbay's 'loyal peer'). The suzerain-side events are mamluk-sultanate's (vassal_start 1433, vassal_end 1472); the shape is unchanged by them.

correction.text: Diyar Bakr without Iraq and Khuzestan

keyframe_review.note: Same grid cells as 1440 (233,249 km2) with the same fault: Iraq belonged to Jahan Shah's Qara Qoyunlu. 1452 is Uzun Hasan's coup at Âmid ('autumn of 1452'); the infobox dates reunification to 1457.

correction.text: Diyar Bakr without Iraq and Khuzestan

keyframe_review.note: Same fault as 1440-1458 (233,176 km2). The Jahan Shah page has Uzun Hasan capturing Amid in 1457.

correction.text: Diyar Bakr, Harput from 1465, without Iraq

keyframe_review.note: 181,432 km2 still carries middle Iraq (Babil, Karbala, Qadisiyyah) that the Qara Qoyunlu held until 1468 (Qara Qoyunlu page: 1464 Baghdad rulers expelled, 1468 Aq Qoyunlu take Iraq). Harput is listed under Uzun Hasan's Dulkadir war in 1465. Correction removes Iraq and Khuzestan.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1468 shape (Diyar Bakr, Iraq, Azerbaijan, Kordestan, Zanjan) plus the central-Iranian provinces of the dissolved Qara Qoyunlu: Hamadan, Qazvin, Qom, Markazi (Saveh), Esfahan, Yazd, Fars (Shiraz) and Kerman

keyframe_review.note: Repaired after review. Cliopatria's 697,815 km2 (2,709 cells) carries Iraq, Azerbaijan, Kordestan and Zanjan added to Diyar Bakr, matching the page's phrase 'By 1468 ... the Aq Qoyunlu defeated the Qara Qoyunlu and conquered Iraq, Azerbaijan, and western Iran' (Qara Qoyunlu page), and Tabriz becomes the capital in 1468 (infobox). It leaves out the plateau that qara-qoyunlu_1453 and _1463 hold (Hamadan, Qazvin, Qom, Markazi, Esfahan, Yazd, Fars, Kerman), which would then be drawn by nobody 1468-1474 although the Qara Qoyunlu state ends in 1468. Corrected from 1468 by adding those eight provinces (2,464 more cells, about 5,170 cells and 1.3 M km2 by cell count). Evidence: the Aq Qoyunlu page speaks of 'Uzun Hasan's conquest of most of mainland Iran' and of Aq Qoyunlu rule in Isfahan (inscription 1475-76) and Fars (Khalil as governor), none with a year; the Uzun Hasan page quotes Contarini, 'Uzun-Hassan took the kingdom of Persia from Causa [Hasan Ali], whom he put to death' (no year); Timurid and Qara Qoyunlu pages give central Iran to Jahan Shah in 1447-1453, so nobody else holds it in 1468. No page dates the passage of Fars, Isfahan, Yazd or Kerman: 1468 is the dissolve year of qara-qoyunlu and a modelling choice, and the Qara Qoyunlu page's Hasan Ali in Fars and Qasim Beg at Kerman (both undated) may have held out into 1469 (Qarabagh, 5 February 1469 in the timurid-empire dossier).

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1475 shape without Gilan, Mazandaran, Semnan and Sistan and Baluchestan (the south-eastern reach to 61 E); Tehran and Alborz stay as part of Iraq-i Ajam

keyframe_review.note: Repaired after review. Cliopatria's 1,701,512 km2 (6,685 cells) covers all of western, central and southern Iran, Iraq and Kuwait. The page confirms Isfahan (Jameh Mosque inscription 1475-76), Fars, Kerman and Iraq-i Ajam as held until the Safavid conquest of 1503 ('He conquered Iraq-Ajami, Fars and Kerman in the summer of 1503'), Hormuz as recognising Aq Qoyunlu suzerainty and Herat held only in July 1470; its lead says the Aq Qoyunlu 'in their last decades also ruled Armenia, Azerbaijan, much of Iran, Iraq, and Oman'. It names none of Gilan (82% of the province in the shape), Mazandaran (61%), Semnan (59%) or Sistan and Baluchestan (34%, the reach to 61 E), and no page opened gives an Aq Qoyunlu governor, campaign or year there, so they are cut (about 6,150 cells, 1.57 M km2 by cell count remain). Tehran and Alborz are kept as the Ray district of Iraq-i Ajam: that is my reading of the term, not a page's statement. The infobox has no area figure, so no ratio can be taken. The step from the corrected 1468 shape to this one is the c1 gain of /ledger/12.

correction.text: the 1502 shape without Gilan, Mazandaran, Semnan and Sistan and Baluchestan, for 1502 only; replaced from 1503 by aq-qoyunlu_1503

keyframe_review.note: 1,542,552 km2. Holds for 1502 only: Azerbaijan fell to Ismail in July 1501 (the shape has already lost it) but 'Summer 1503: Iraq-Ajami, Fars, and Kerman conquered' (Aq Qoyunlu page; Hamadan 1503 on the Ismail I page). 1503-1506 is the new keyframe aq-qoyunlu_1503. Same trim as aq-qoyunlu_1475 (no page names those four provinces as Aq Qoyunlu land): about 5,570 cells remain.

correction.text: Mesopotamia and Diyar Bakr without Iran

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: after the summer of 1503 the Aq Qoyunlu hold Iraq, Diyar Bakr and the Jazira ('Iranian collapse'; Murad retreats to Diyar Bakr), until Diyarbakir falls in 1507-08 and Baghdad in 1508.

350,485 km2: Iraq and Diyar Bakr. The shape stands for 1507-1508 only: Ismail and Husayn Beg Shamlu 'seized Baghdad' in 1508, 'putting an end to the Aq Qoyunlu' (Ismail I page, no month). Cliopatria runs the row to 1511; the dossier ends in 1508. The years 1509-1511 belong to the Safavids in Iraq; the Ottoman takeover of Diyar Bakr is not dated on any page opened.

ledger.note: 1378: Qara Yuluk Uthman Beg founds the Aq Qoyunlu confederation (infobox 'Established: 1378'; 'Founded in the Diyarbakir region by Qara Yuluk Uthman Beg and ruled eastern Turkey from 1378 to 1508'). Core drawn at Bayburt, where the page attests them in the 1340s.
1402: Timur grants Diyar Bakr to Kara Yuluk Osman ('Timur granted them Diyar Bakr in 1402'); Mardin is part of the Diyarbakır governorship (Uzun Hasan page).
1403: Âmid (Diyarbakır) becomes the capital and the Aq Qoyunlu become sultans (infobox 'Âmid (1403-1468)').

region.text: the Syrian Jazira south of Diyar Bakr

ledger.note: Page silent: Cliopatria's 1415 shape adds about 20,000 km2 in Raqqa and Hasakah (Syria) to the Diyar Bakr core; no page opened dates or explains it. Counterpart is a guess from the border (Mamluk Syria). Reviewed 2026-10-25: the Mamluk Sultanate page does not mention Raqqa, Hasakah or Diyar Bakr and names no holder in 1407-1415. Its only related lines are the 'rise of Turkmen tribes in the Jazira' under Faraj and the Mamluk reprisals 'in response to Aq Qoyonlu raids against the Jazira' (Edessa 1429, Amid 1433), which make an Aq Qoyunlu presence in the Jazira before 1429 plausible but date nothing. Stays confidence 1; the counterpart stays the border guess.
1465: Uzun Hasan captures Harput (listed under his war with Dulkadir: 'he captured Harput in 1465').

region.text: the sanjak of Capakcur near Bingol and Mush

ledger.note: 30 October (or 11 November) 1467: Uzun Hasan defeats and kills Jahan Shah at the Battle of Chapakchur, near Bingol. Jahan Shah's 1466 advance had reached Mush.
1468: the Qara Qoyunlu collapse ('the collapse of the Qara Qoyunlu control in the Middle East'; Hasan Ali's brief reign 1467-68).
1468: 'Aq Qoyunlu defeated the Qara Qoyunlu and took Iraq, Azerbaijan and western Iran'. Tabriz becomes the capital (infobox 'Tabriz (1468 - 6 January 1478)').

region.text: the central-Iranian provinces of the Qara Qoyunlu: Hamadan, Qazvin, Qom, Saveh, Isfahan, Yazd, Fars (Shiraz) and Kerman

ledger.note: 1468: the plateau Jahan Shah took in 1447-1453 passes to Uzun Hasan with the end of the Qara Qoyunlu ('By 1468 ... the Aq Qoyunlu defeated the Qara Qoyunlu and conquered Iraq, Azerbaijan, and western Iran', Qara Qoyunlu page). The Aq Qoyunlu page speaks of 'Uzun Hasan's conquest of most of mainland Iran' (no year) and attests Isfahan in 1475-76 and Khalil as Aq Qoyunlu governor of Fars; the Uzun Hasan page has 'Uzun-Hassan took the kingdom of Persia from Causa [Hasan Ali], whom he put to death' (no year). No page dates Fars, Isfahan, Yazd or Kerman, so 1468 is qara-qoyunlu's dissolve year and the provinces are my reading of 'western Iran' and 'most of mainland Iran' (confidence 2). Hasan Ali in Fars and Qasim Beg at Kerman are undated on the Qara Qoyunlu page, so the last holdouts may run into 1469 (Qarabagh, 1469).
1468: the seat moves from Âmid to Tabriz (infobox 'Tabriz (1468 - 6 January 1478)').

July 1470: Uzun Hasan temporarily captures Herat from Sultan Husayn Bayqara ('Herat temporarily captured from Sultan Husayn Bayqara (Khorasan)'). The month is kept in this note only because the withdrawal has no date and the ledger must stay in order.
1470: the capture of Herat is only 'temporary'; the page gives no date for the withdrawal.

region.text: the Gulf coast and the Zagros edge (Hormozgan, Bushehr, Khuzestan, Lorestan, Ilam, Kermanshah, Chahar Mahall and Bakhtiari, Kohgiluyeh and Buyer Ahmad) and Tehran with Alborz

ledger.note: Page silent on who held these lands and when the Aq Qoyunlu took them: the step from the corrected 1468 shape to Cliopatria's 1475 shape adds about 1,070 cells (270,000 km2) here, to within 30 cells of fringe, none of them in a Qara Qoyunlu shape of the dossier set. The page attests only Isfahan (1475-76) and Iraq-i Ajam, Fars and Kerman held to 1503, and says the Aq Qoyunlu 'in their last decades also ruled Armenia, Azerbaijan, much of Iran, Iraq, and Oman'. 'nobody' means no state of the dossier set, not a claim that the land was stateless. Placed at the start of the 1475 shape.

Page silent on the year: the lead says Hormuz 'recognized Aq Qoyunlu suzerainty'; placed where Cliopatria's shape reaches the Gulf coast. Reviewed 2026-10-25: the Kingdom of Ormus page does not mention the Aq Qoyunlu or Uzun Hasan; it says only that Hormuz stood 'under the suzerainty of kings of Iran from the foundation of the kingdom in the 11th century' (no dynasty named) and that Portugal landed in September 1507 and held Ormuz from 1515. The year stays a placement (confidence 1).

July 1501: Ismail occupies Tabriz after defeating the Aq Qoyunlu ruler Alvand at Sharur ('After occupying Tabriz, Ismail took the title Padshah-i Iran'); the Aq Qoyunlu page dates the Iranian collapse to autumn 1501. The province is my reading of Tabriz.

region.text: Iraq-i Ajam, Fars, Kerman and the rest of Iran in the corrected 1502 shape

ledger.note: Summer 1503: 'Iraq-Ajami, Fars, and Kerman conquered' by Ismail (Hamadan 1503 on the Ismail I page). The rest of the Iranian part of the 1502 shape is my reading: Cliopatria's 1507 shape no longer has it. Gilan, Mazandaran, Semnan and Sistan and Baluchestan are left out, as in the corrected 1502 keyframe.

Page silent: Hormuz's recognition of Aq Qoyunlu suzerainty lapses with the loss of Fars and Kerman in 1503; no page says so. The Kingdom of Ormus page (read 2026-10-25) is silent on the Aq Qoyunlu and on any 1503 change, so the end stays a placement.
1507-1508: Diyarbakir passes to the Safavids ('1507-1508 Diyarbakir', via the Mowsillu; the Ismail I page dates Diyarbakir to 1507 without naming the Aq Qoyunlu).
Autumn 1508: Ismail and Husayn Beg Shamlu seize Baghdad and Mesopotamia ('Autumn 1508: Mesopotamia'; Ismail I page: Baghdad seized 1508, 'putting an end to the Aq Qoyunlu').
1508: the Aq Qoyunlu end ('putting an end to the Aq Qoyunlu', Baghdad seized 1508); the Aq Qoyunlu page: collapse in Iran 1503, end in Mesopotamia 1508. Cliopatria carries the row to 1511.

wars.name: Uzun Hasan's war with Dulkadir over Harput
Qara Qoyunlu-Aq Qoyunlu war
wars.outcome: Jahan Shah's 1466 advance reaches Mush and withdraws; Uzun Hasan wins at Chapakchur (30 October or 11 November 1467) and takes Iraq, Azerbaijan and western Iran by 1468.

wars.name: Battle of Qarabagh (Aq Qoyunlu-Timurid war)
wars.outcome: Abu Sa'id Mirza is defeated at the Battle of Qarabagh in 1469 and executed; no frontier changes.
wars.note: The Timurid dossier dates the start to February 1468; this page gives the year of Qarabagh only.

wars.name: Aq Qoyunlu capture of Herat
wars.outcome: Herat temporarily captured from Sultan Husayn Bayqara in July 1470.

wars.name: Ottoman-Aq Qoyunlu war
wars.outcome: Uzun Hasan advances to Akşehir and pillages Tokat in 1471, fights at Tercan and is defeated at Otlukbeli in late summer 1473 by Mehmed II; the pages record no border change.
wars.note: Aq Qoyunlu page: 'defeat by the Ottomans at Otlukbeli' 1473; Karamanids allied against the Ottomans, undated.

wars.name: Aq Qoyunlu succession wars
belligerents: rival Aq Qoyunlu claimants (Rustam, Baysungur, Ahmad Bey, Alvand, Murad)
wars.outcome: Khalil (a few months in 1478), Ya'qub (1478-1490), Rustam, Baysungur (dethroned 1491, killed 1493) and Ahmad Bey (died December 1497) fight for the throne; the realm divides among rival rulers (Alvand, Qasim, Mohammad, Murad) after Ahmad's death. Battle of Khoy July 1478.
wars.note: Rustam's reign is 1478-1490 in one passage and 1493-1496 elsewhere on the page. No border change is dated.

wars.name: Safavid conquest of the Aq Qoyunlu

zones.text: the Iranian part of the corrected 1502 shape

wars.outcome: Ismail wins at Sharur (1501), occupies Tabriz (July 1501), defeats an Aq Qoyunlu army in 1502, takes Iraq-i Ajam and Fars after Hamadan and Kerman (summer 1503), Diyarbakir (1507-08) and Baghdad (1508).

notes:
Seven pages cited (state article, Uzun Hasan, Ismail I, Qara Qoyunlu, Jahan Shah, and for the repair Mamluk Sultanate and Kingdom of Ormus; the repair pages exceed the budget of five). The Uzun Hasan page is thin on the conquests of Iran and no page opened dates them, so the central-Iranian gain is dated to qara-qoyunlu's dissolve year (1468, confidence 2) and the remainder of the 1475 shape is a confidence-1 event.
Wikidata Q555994: shared with Cliopatria's 'Lu' (-750..-248, the Zhou-era state in Shandong). They are different states; Aq Qoyunlu is a Turkoman confederation of 1378-1508 and the Aq Qoyunlu page never mentions a Lu. One of the two rows carries a wrong id; Wikidata is unreachable, so which is not settled here. The Aq Qoyunlu dossier keeps Q555994 as Cliopatria gives it.
Cliopatria problems: (1) the 1440-1467 shapes (233k and 181k km2) carry lower and middle Iraq and Khuzestan, overlapping the area of the 'Hashemite Arab Federation' row (1415-1439), which is really the Jalayirid remnant (to 1432) and then Qara Qoyunlu land; removed by correction. (2) The 1502-1506 shape keeps Iran after the Safavid conquest of 1503. (3) The row runs to 1511, the pages end the state in 1508. (4) The shape for 1415-1439 adds Raqqa and Hasakah (Syria) with no page behind it. (5) The state is drawn from 1407, the page says 1378.
Not settled: the order of Uzun Hasan's coup (autumn 1452 at Âmid, Uzun Hasan page footnote) against 'reunification 1457' (infobox) and Jahan Shah's capture of Amid in 1457 by Uzun Hasan (Jahan Shah page); the dates of the conquests of Isfahan, Fars, Yazd, Kerman and the Khorasan fringes (none on any page; drawn from 1468); the Mamluk suzerainty (the Mamluk dossier has vassal_start 1433 and vassal_end 1472; the Aq Qoyunlu page calls Qaitbay Uzun Hasan's 'loyal peer'); the Hormuz suzerainty (undated); the Ottoman takeover of Diyar Bakr (Ismail I page dates Diyarbakir to 1507 but not to the Aq Qoyunlu); Shirvan tribute (Contarini quoted on the Uzun Hasan page: 'Media ... under subjection to Sivansa, who pays a kind of yearly tribute'), not drawn. Rulers: the infobox and text give Kara Yuluk 1378-1435, Uzun Hasan 1452-1478 but nothing for 1435-1452, and the later reigns are contradictory (Rustam), so no ruler strip.
Vassal relations of this state as the vassal (Timurids 1402 grant, Mamluks 1433-1472) belong to the overlords' dossiers.
Counterparts: Kingdom of Hormuz (vassal 1475-1503, confidence 1) needs a dossier if the map is to show it. Gazetteer: every name resolves.
Repair after review (2026-10-25): (1) the conquest of Hamadan, Qazvin, Qom, Saveh, Isfahan, Yazd, Fars and Kerman is now a 1468 gain from qara-qoyunlu (confidence 2), so the land does not stand undrawn from 1468 to 1474 and pairs with qara-qoyunlu's 1468 dissolve; aq-qoyunlu_1468 is adjust (Cliopatria's shape plus those provinces). (2) aq-qoyunlu_1475 and _1502 are adjust: Gilan, Mazandaran, Semnan and Sistan and Baluchestan are cut because no page names them (Tehran and Alborz kept as Iraq-i Ajam, my reading); the 1503 loss and the Safavid war zone follow the same trim; the 1475 gain of the Gulf coast and Zagros edge (about 270,000 km2, counterpart 'nobody', confidence 1) explains the rest of the step to Cliopatria's 1475 shape. (3) Thin items re-read: the Mamluk Sultanate page is silent on Raqqa and Hasakah (the 1415 gain stays confidence 1); the Kingdom of Ormus page is silent on the Aq Qoyunlu (the Hormuz pair stays confidence 1, 1475-1503); no page gives Aq Qoyunlu holdings for 1435-1452 beyond Diyar Bakr, and the Mamluk Sultanate page confirms the recognition of Mamluk suzerainty after 1433 without a year or an end. Not done: qara-qoyunlu's own 1468 loss (/ledger/29) still names Cliopatria's 1467 shape and not the central-Iranian provinces; that dossier is outside this repair and needs the matching region.
